title.contents: Philosophy of religion: Hume and Kierkegaard

audience.contents: Undergraduate philosophy students writing for an educated reader unfamiliar with these thinkers.

contents: Create a focused comparative assignment that requires interpretation and evaluation, not two disconnected summaries.
Require a defensible thesis, fair treatment of both thinkers, and engagement with a plausible objection.
Ask for textual support without inventing quotations, page numbers, or required editions.
Reward accurate interpretation, substantive comparison, and reasoned evaluation rather than agreement with a particular religious position.

interpretation.description: Accurately explains each thinker's arguments and relevant concepts.

comparison.description: Develops a shared question and explains meaningful similarities and differences.

evidence.description: Supports interpretations with relevant primary-text passages and distinguishes authors from speakers or pseudonymous voices where relevant.

argument.description: Defends a clear thesis, evaluates arguments, and addresses an objection.
